reference: Numerics @ 2a0357a. Runs corehydro::numerics::support::run_callback (core/include/corehydro/numerics/support/callback_runner.hpp), group "math", against the callback named by `construct.callback` -- a function each of the four runners writes itself as a native closure (a C++ lambda, an R closure, a Python lambda, a C# delegate), so every case exercises the real host-language callback path the runner's guard exists to protect. NOTE the catalog names here are NOT the `optimizer`-kind catalog's: `Diff_FXYZ` is Test_Differentiation.FXYZ (x^3 + y^4 + z^5), not the unrelated TestFunctions.FXYZ the optimizer fixtures use. Every expected value and tolerance is the upstream MSTest `Assert.AreEqual(expected, actual, delta)` literal, transcribed verbatim, EXCEPT the assertions whose `source` opens with EMITTER-READ: no upstream test reads AdaptiveGaussKronrod's FunctionEvaluations, StandardError or Status, so those are read off the REAL C# library through tools/oracle_emitter instead. Neither kind is ever a value computed by this repo's own C++. `Quad_Peak` is likewise a corehydro addition rather than an upstream integrand: every Integrands.cs function the upstream tests integrate converges on the first whole-interval evaluation at 21 function evaluations, so without it the subdividing branch of the recursion has no oracle at all. `quadrature_nd_pi`/`quadrature_miser_gsl`/`quadrature_vegas_sum_normals` (P2 "math extras", Task 6) are ALL EMITTER-READ: the upstream Test_MonteCarlo/Test_Miser/Test_Vegas methods are loose true-value checks (1e-2 to 1e-3 relative), so the pinned values here are the SEEDED C# result at the option settings each case's `options` carries -- chosen small so the gate stays fast -- not the upstream literal.

Looser than every other tolerance in this file (measured drift ~1.1e-7 relative, not sub-ulp): chi_squared is `(sum_chi_squared_ - sum_weighted_results_ * result_) / (it + 1)`, a subtraction of two close large quantities that AMPLIFIES the ~1-ulp difference between clang/gcc's default fused-multiply-add contraction (core/CMakeLists.txt's -ffp-contract=off is deliberately scoped to the fixture_callback_catalog.cpp TU alone, NOT the shared core Vegas/Miser/MonteCarloIntegration classes, so R, Python and this C++ runner all compile and AGREE with each other on the fused arithmetic, but not with .NET's never-fused one) and .NET's own never-fused arithmetic; isolated single-file recompiles of vegas.hpp confirm removing contraction there reproduces the C# value to the bit, and restoring it reproduces this file's own pinned value to the bit -- a measured toolchain effect, not a stream/order bug
